text:
Predicates:
CanRegisterVote(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipateElection2024(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasUSCitizenship(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegisterVote(x) → ParticipateElection2024(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasUSCitizenship(x) → CanRegisterVote(x) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (HasUSCitizenship(x) ∨ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(x)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(HasTaiwaneseCitizenship(Vladimir) ∨ Manager(Vladimir, Gazprom)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegisterVote(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
